rejected.detail: stock too high-priced for current account size, cannot fit even minimum scaled position. Gate 3: risk_dollars=$250, risk_per_share=$6.75, quantity=37 shares, notional=$13,144 (52.6% of account) — far above the 15% standard cap ($3,750). Small-scaled exception: max M=floor($5,000/$355.25)=14 shares, notional=$4,973.50 (under 20% extended cap), but risk_M=14×$6.75=$94.50 < risk_dollars_floor=0.40×$250=$100.00. M=15 would satisfy the 40% risk floor (risk=$101.25) but pushes notional to $5,328.75 > $5,000 extended cap. No integer M exists satisfying both constraints simultaneously.

summary: CPAY rejected at Gate 4 (single_position_cap_exceeded): at ~$355/share, the minimum-viable scaled position (14 shares, $4,974 notional) uses only $94.50 of risk vs. the $100 floor required by the small-scaled exception, and 15 shares pushes notional above the 20% extended cap. Despite a genuinely strong setup — Gates 0–3 all pass (direction consensus clean, budget open, expected return +$5.19/share from combined_p_bull=0.519 vs. bears' 0.481, positive post-earnings drift thesis with ADX_14=30.49 and guidance raise) — the discrete-share math on a $25k account cannot accommodate a $355 stock within the position-cap rules.
